課程綱要.課程目標: Course Introduction Programming is one of the most essential skills for EE/CS students, enabling them to tackle complex engineering problems. This course provides in-depth knowledge of C++ programming alongside systematic problem-solving skills. We anticipate that most students will have little to no prior programming experience. Therefore, the course begins with the fundamentals of C++ syntax and programming concepts, followed by detailed explanations of the underlying principles. Students will not only learn the theory but also practice implementation through individual programming assignments. Special Notes for Students This course is designed primarily for first-year EE students and has strong connections with other EE courses. Please expect to spend a significant amount of time on programming practice and reading supplementary materials. We strongly recommend taking the Introduction to Computer Science Laboratory course concurrently, as its exercises will directly support your programming assignments. Students from other departments should carefully consider enrolling, as this is a heavy-loaded course. You may need to acquire relevant EE domain knowledge on your own. Why Programming Matters for AI and IC Design In technology landscape nowadays, programming is a cornerstone skill for rapidly growing fields such as artificial intelligence (AI) and integrated circuit (IC) design. In AI, programming is essential for implementing algorithms, training and optimizing models, and processing massive datasets efficiently. In IC and computer-aided design (CAD) for circuits, programming enables the development of simulation tools, automated design flows, and hardware–software co-optimization. By mastering C++, a language widely used in high-performance computing, you will gain a solid foundation to handle computationally intensive tasks and develop tools for both AI applications and chip design automation. These skills are critical for staying competitive in modern engineering careers. Learning Outcomes By the end of the course, you will: - Understand how a program works and what constitutes good coding style and habits. - Be able to derive algorithms and implement them in C++ to solve complex problems. - Recognize how programming can be applied to other EE domains, including AI and IC design. - Gain deeper insights into programming concepts, which will benefit you when learning other languages such as Python or Java. - Develop strong self-learning skills to help you solve problems independently in the future. Note that this is an in-depth course, so you will be expected to engage with the material at a deeper level than in standard C++ courses. The additional details and concepts covered here will serve as a valuable foundation for your future programming and engineering endeavors.

課程綱要.課程目標: 電路 I 和 II 的主要目標是讓學生掌握分析由被動元件（例如: 電阻器、電容器、電感器和變壓器）和主動元件（例如: 運算放大器）組成的電路的基本知識和技能。
課程綱要.授課內容: 在電路 I 中，當訊號為直流或階躍函數時，我們將學習如何計算流經每個元件的電流和每個節點的電壓，所使用的電路分析技巧包括: KCL/KVL、current/voltage dividers、Wheatstone bridges、delta-to-wye equivalent circuits、node-voltage、mesh-current、Thevenin/Norton equivalent circuits、superposition、virtual short of OP amp、natural/step responses of RLC circuits等。在電路 II 中，當訊號變為交流電時，我們將首先學習如何使用Phasor（即僅考慮振幅和相位），同時搭配在電路 I 中所學習的技巧來分析特定頻率下的電路。接下來，當訊號是頻率變化的正弦波時，我們將學習如何使用Laplace轉換來獲得頻率響應，以及如何建立低通、高通和帶通濾波器。

課程綱要.授課內容: 在電路 I 中，當訊號為直流或階躍函數時，我們將學習如何計算流經每個元件的電流和每個節點的電壓，所使用的電路分析技巧包括: KCL/KVL、current/voltage dividers、Wheatstone bridges、delta-to-wye equivalent circuits、node-voltage、mesh-current、Thevenin/Norton equivalent circuits、superposition、virtual short of OP amp、natural/step responses of RLC circuits等。在電路 II 中，當訊號變為交流電時，我們將首先學習如何使用Phasor（即僅考慮振幅和相位），同時搭配在電路 I 中所學習的技巧來分析特定頻率下的電路。接下來，當訊號是頻率變化的正弦波時，我們將學習如何使用Laplace轉換來獲得頻率響應，以及如何建立低通、高通和帶通濾波器。

課程綱要.課程目標: “工程數學-複變”之主要課程內容為”複變函數分析”。複變函數為一種很特殊，亦很有用的函數。它具有純量值函數及向量值函數之雙重性，亦就是說複變函數可視為如實數般的純量，亦可視為如二維向量般的向量。因此我們在學過“實變函數分析”及“向量函數的分析”後，須再學習複變函數的分析，包括其微分與積分。在電機工程的許多基礎課程中，如電路學、電磁學、控制系統與通訊系統等課程均涉及複變函數的應用，例如可藉由複變函數簡便地表示交流電壓、電流與頻域阻抗等，從而降低問題分析的複雜度。因此，複變函數分析對於電機工程系的學生而言是重要的基礎。
課程綱要.授課內容:
“課程大綱：
Unit 0: Introduction
Unit 1: Complex Numbers and Functions. Complex Differentiation
Unit 2: Complex Integration
Unit 3: Power Series. Taylor Series
Unit 4: Laurent Series. Residue Integration
Unit 5: Conformal Mapping
Unit 6: Complex Analysis Applied to Potential Theory“
課程綱要.教科書/參考書: “Reference: Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10e., Wiley. Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 6th ed. by D. G. Zill and W. S. Wright. Brown and Churchill, Complex Variables and Applications, 8th ed., McGraw Hill“

課程綱要.課程目標: This class will cover some special topics in the field of signal integrity (SI) and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), including transmission line theory, causality theory, and power integrity, as detailed in the course content below. While transmission line and power integrity are important subjects specific for SI engineers, causality is a topic that also finds broad applications in other branches of physics. The theories of these topics will be introduced in class, and students are required to complete several homework which are mostly Python-coding problems (but not exclusively). This course is not a sequel of the course Signal Integrity and Electromagnetic Compatibility of the spring semester, so students are welcome to take this course even if you have not taken the spring-semester one. Undergraduates are also welcome to take this course as long as you have studied 電磁學, 複變, and 信號與系統.
課程綱要.授課內容:
1. Numerical inverse Fourier transform
2. Transmission line theory
* Exact TEM mode
* Dielectric model
* Quasi-TEM mode
* Conductor model
* TDR
* Surface roughness
* Multi-conductor line
* Modal decomposition
* Crosstalk
3. Causality
* Causality theorems
* Causality assessment
4. Power integrity
* Power delivery framework
* Buck converter analysis and design
* PDN analysis and design
課程綱要.教科書/參考書: 1. Stephen Hall and Howard Heck, Advanced Signal Integrity for High Speed Digital Designs, Wiley-IEEE Press, 2009. ( https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/book/5361024 ) 2. Clayton Paul, Introduction to Electromagnetic Compatibility, Wiley, 2005. ( https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/0471758159 ) Both books can be downloaded if you are within NCU‘s ip. 3. M. Swaminathan and A. Engin, Power Integrity Modeling and Design for Semiconductors and Systems, Prentice Hall, 2008. (Available at library) 4. Eric Bogatin, Signal and Power Integrity – Simplified, 2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 2010, Ch 13. (Available at library) 5. S. Grivet-Talocia and B. Gustavsen, Passive macromodeling: Theory and applications, John Wiley ＆ Sons, 2016. (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/book/10.1002/9781119140931)

If the selected students are absent, they will get 0 score for that homework. Also note that the reports of all students of all homework will be open for every one in class to view, in the eeclass system.

光纖通信系統基本架構介紹 I

光纖通信調變技術介紹II
